justification: Closes the cross-property mix-up in the PDF report (the /conveyancing/pdf twin of #811). generate_conveyancing_pdf's cache-miss path trusted the caller's prop_id (int(req.prop_id)) for controls/valuation while using req.lat/req.lng for every spatial fetch, so a direct caller could blend one property's controls with another's overlays/DAs/hazards. The cache-miss path now binds prop_id, coordinates and lot_wkt via _resolve_property (the #811 helper); all spatial fetches use the bound lat/lng (no req.lat/req.lng remain in the handler); and a cache entry lacking its own authoritative coordinates is treated as a miss and fully re-resolved rather than paired with request-supplied coordinates. Operational resolver failures return 503 via _resolve_property.

pre_impl.existing_data: Reuses _resolve_property (merged in #811) and the existing pipeline cache written by run_conveyancing's _save_pipeline_cache, which already stores address, prop_id, lat, lng and lot_wkt. No new data source, query, or fetcher is introduced.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Confirmed the frontend reaches this endpoint with a report_id whose cache was written by the authoritative free-tier run, so the normal flow always hits the coordinate-bearing cache branch; the caller-triple path is a direct-API vector. All 14 req.lat/req.lng usages were inside generate_conveyancing_pdf only, so rebinding them to a local lat/lng is safe.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New: the cache-miss _resolve_property binding, the local lat/lng rebinding of every spatial fetch, and the cache-hit guard requiring cached coordinates. Deliberately unchanged: the cache-hit unpacking of controls/valuation/overlays, the parallel PDF-exclusive fetchers, and _resolve_property itself.

functions.name: generate_conveyancing_pdf
functions.input: a ConveyancingPdfRequest (address, report_id, and advisory lat/lng/prop_id); the property is taken from the coordinate-bearing pipeline cache or, on a miss, from _resolve_property(req)
functions.output: a generated PDF whose LEP controls, valuation, overlays, strata, DAs and hazards all describe the one resolved property; the advisory caller lat/lng/prop_id are never used for any fetch
functions.if_none: on a cache miss with an unresolvable address _resolve_property raises HTTPException 422, and 503 on a resolver outage; a cache entry missing lat/lng is treated as a miss and fully re-resolved

values: N/A - reads no DB or API values directly; wraps the existing pipeline cache and _resolve_property.
queries: N/A - no SQL is written or changed in this diff.

break_it.scenario: A direct /conveyancing/pdf caller submits a report_id with no cache entry, an address for property B, but a prop_id for property A.
break_it.what_happens: The old cache-miss path set resolved_prop_id from int(req.prop_id) (A) for controls and valuation while every spatial fetch used req.lat/req.lng (B), producing a PDF blending two properties.
break_it.how: The cache-miss branch now calls _resolve_property(req), which derives prop_id, coordinates and lot_wkt from the one address and ignores the caller triple; all fetches use the bound lat/lng.

break_it.scenario: A caller submits a report_id whose cached entry is an older one lacking lat/lng, together with a different property's address.
break_it.what_happens: An earlier version of this fix fell back to resolving coordinates from req.address while keeping the cached property's controls, so a mismatched report_id and address could still blend two properties.
break_it.how: The cache-hit guard now requires the entry's own lat and lng to be present; an entry missing them falls through to the full authoritative re-resolution, so cached controls are never paired with separately-resolved coordinates.

break_it.scenario: A future edit wires a new spatial fetcher in the PDF handler using req.lat / req.lng directly.
break_it.what_happens: That fetch would run at the caller-supplied coordinates rather than the resolved property's, silently reintroducing the mix-up for that data source.
break_it.how: An AST guard asserts generate_conveyancing_pdf reads no req.lat / req.lng anywhere in code; every coordinate is the bound lat/lng.

break_it.scenario: A future edit reintroduces int(req.prop_id) to derive the property in the PDF handler.
break_it.what_happens: Controls and valuation would again come from the caller-supplied prop_id, decoupled from the coordinates used for spatial data.
break_it.how: An AST guard asserts the handler never reads req.prop_id; the property comes from the cache or _resolve_property.
